notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Financial figures are from the FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0001193125-26-071966, filed February 25, 2026) and ownership from the 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001308179-26-000262, filed April 10, 2026, shares as of March 31, 2026), both filed under CIK 0002012383. BlackRock completed the HPS acquisition in July 2025, paying substantially all consideration in Class B-2 common units of a consolidated subsidiary, BlackRock Saturn Subco, LLC ('Subco Units'), exchangeable one-for-one into common stock. LARRY FINK (Chairman and CEO): 250,119 shares plus 14,297 deferred/restricted units and options; less than 1% (marked * in the proxy), so pctEconomic is null. HOLDERS: the 2026 proxy lists only two holders above 5%, BlackRock's own funds (6.17%) and the Kuwait Investment Authority (5.14%); Vanguard, at 8.31% in the 2025 proxy, is no longer listed. The proxy gives the 13G filing dates (BlackRock February 9, 2024; KIA July 7, 2020), not their as-of dates, so asOf is null and both figures are old. DIVIDENDS: $3,265 million declared to BlackRock stockholders ($20.84 per share), from the equity statement. The cash-flow line 'Dividends/Subco distributions paid' ($3,347 million) also includes $82 million of distributions to Subco unit holders, which are recorded as redeemable noncontrolling interests, so it is not used (the two reconcile exactly). BUYBACKS: the cash-flow line ($1,951 million) combines common shares, Subco units and shares withheld for employee taxes; the equity statement shows $1,374 million of shares repurchased, $251 million of Subco units and $326 million of employee tax withholdings, and the MD&A says the company 'repurchased an aggregate of 1.6 million shares and share equivalents for approximately $1.6 billion' under its program. The combined cash line is used. Neither cash line has a standard XBRL concept (BlackRock tags them with its own blk: elements), so no xbrl object is attached. STOCK COMP: $1,307 million, including incentive retention awards granted in connection with the HPS and GIP transactions. GEOGRAPHY is by the legal entity that books the revenue, not customer location (Americas mainly the U.S.; Europe mainly the UK, Luxembourg and the Netherlands).

ecosystem.notes: AUM is a stock of client money, not a flow, so no take rate is computed on it. BlackRock's fee is the platform's share of client returns: the 10-K says "Investment management fees are typically earned as a percentage of AUM", and BlackRock also earns performance fees and technology services (Aladdin) revenue. The investment returns on the AUM belong to BlackRock's clients. The 10-K describes it as "$14.0 trillion of assets under management ("AUM") at December 31, 2025"; the increase from $11.6 trillion includes AUM acquired with HPS (July 2025) and ElmTree (September 2025).
